issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires calculateTotalPrice to be static (lines specifying which methods/attributes must be static), but both the provided template Main (calls shop.calculateTotalPrice(...)) and the solution implement calculateTotalPrice as an instance method (non-static). This creates a cross-artifact inconsistency: students reading the problem will be told to make the method static, while the example usage in Main and the reference solution use it as an instance method. This may confuse students about the correct signature and where to place the method (static vs instance) and may cause mismatch with any tests or example code.
issues.suggested_fix: Make artifacts consistent: either (A) update the problem statement to not require calculateTotalPrice to be static (so an instance method is acceptable), or (B) change the template and solution to declare calculateTotalPrice as static and update example usage in Main to call SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(...). Prefer updating the problem statement to remove the 'static' requirement if the intended examples and solution should treat it as an instance method.

issues.description: The problem text instructs that the attributes (orders and stock) should be initialized to default values in the SealSaloon constructor (constructor takes no parameters). Immediately afterwards it also requires that the stock attribute be static (shared across instances). These two instructions conflict: a static final field cannot be properly initialized per-instance in an instance constructor (and static final must be assigned at declaration or in a static initializer). This is a structural contradiction that will confuse students about where/how to initialize the shared stock field and may block correct implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify intended design in the problem statement: if stock should be shared (static), state that stock must be a static (and optionally final) field and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, not in the instance constructor. Alternatively, if the intent is to initialize stock in the constructor (per-instance), remove the requirement that stock be static. Update the problem text so it does not instruct students to initialize a static final field in the instance constructor.
